name: Agentic Scientist
summary: Orchestrates coding agents through investigation, ablations, sealed evaluation, analysis, and manuscript production. The public implementation includes task snapshots, resumable runs, and an inspection interface. It is useful for studying research orchestration and evidence collection; successful execution and scientific validity still depend on the task, evaluator, and underlying agent.

name: OpenResearch
summary: A local research workspace and harness from alphaXiv that connects coding agents to literature discovery, experiment execution, and artifact inspection. It records experiments in a local database and supports multiple compute backends. The repository documents a usable product; these capabilities are project claims rather than an independently established discovery benchmark.

name: ScienceBuddy
summary: Combines an interactive scientific workspace with research on alternating harness improvement and model reinforcement learning. The public repository distinguishes its hosted workspace demonstration from open experiments using frozen tasks and simulated feedback. It is especially relevant to human feedback and persistent research context; deployed continual improvement is not established by the released experiment alone.

name: The AI Scientist
summary: Implements a template-based loop for proposing ideas, changing experimental code, running machine-learning experiments, and drafting papers with an automated reviewer. The repository provides executable workflows and example outputs. Its structured starting templates make it a useful baseline for research automation, while generated manuscripts still require inspection of results, citations, and methodological claims.

name: The AI Scientist-v2
summary: Uses staged tree search, debugging, replication, and visual feedback to develop experiments and manuscripts from supplied research topics. Humans selected three ideas and the best completed outputs for workshop review; one passed, and all were withdrawn under the agreed protocol. Internal audits expose leakage and claim–code mismatches, qualifying the evidence from selected manuscript acceptance.

name: ScientistOne
summary: Links literature, code-search artifacts, and manuscript claims through evidence tags and integrity audits. Adapted ADRS evaluations include human correction of flagged audit results, while majority-vote checks miss a documented exploit. Transfer medal results use repeated test-grader feedback rather than the official single-submission protocol. Generated artifacts and complete framework availability remain separate questions.

name: ScientistTwo
summary: Coordinates limitation-driven hypotheses, experiments, ablations, and simulated review–rebuttal cycles. The study reports 86 successful improvements from 107 selected ML challenges, with most review comparisons conditioned on those successes. Human manuscript assessment adds evidence, while unmatched baseline pools and automated acceptance limit interpretation. Generated research artifacts are distinct from a released orchestration framework.

name: Agent Laboratory
summary: Organizes specialist agents around literature review, planning, experimentation, and reporting for a researcher-supplied idea. The open implementation supports human feedback during the workflow and machine-learning experimentation. It provides a concrete research-assistant baseline; the quality and efficiency claims in its paper should be interpreted within the evaluated tasks and model configurations.

name: Biomni
summary: A biomedical research agent that combines retrieval-guided planning with executable code and a broad scientific software environment. Its repository exposes the agent, environment setup, tutorials, and supported research workflows. It is useful for investigating tool-rich biological analysis; biomedical task demonstrations do not establish clinical safety or reliability across all research domains.

name: Virtual Lab
summary: Structures collaboration between a human researcher and specialist language-model agents through team and individual meetings. The public code includes the nanobody-design application accompanying a Nature study with experimental validation. This supplies a grounded example of collaborative scientific discovery, while the biological evidence applies to that specific campaign rather than unrestricted autonomous laboratory work.

name: Coscientist
summary: Connects language models with literature and documentation search, code execution, and laboratory automation for chemistry tasks. The Nature study demonstrates planning and execution across several experimental settings. The public repository contains supporting data and a simplified implementation, with commercial-use restrictions; it should not be described as a complete unrestricted release of the original laboratory system.

name: Google Co-Scientist
summary: A Gemini-based system in which agents generate, critique, rank, and refine scientific hypotheses in collaboration with researchers. Google describes biological case studies and an experimental Hypothesis Generation access route. This is a hosted research partner focused on hypothesis development; a general open-source implementation of Google's system was not confirmed.

name: Kosmos
summary: Coordinates parallel literature and data-analysis agents through a persistent world model. Seven selected studies include reproduced findings and new hypotheses, assessed through sampled human reanalysis and external validation. Researchers curate inputs, one final report is manually assembled, and productivity equivalents are collaborator estimates. Traceable artifacts support scrutiny without guaranteeing every interpretation or a general discovery yield.

name: ResearchStudio
summary: Microsoft’s ResearchStudio provides Idea for literature-grounded proposal development and Reel for editable posters, narrated videos, blogs, and an aligned viewer. Idea is assessed through automated proposal judgments; Reel’s quantitative study covers posters, while other outputs remain capability demonstrations. Their shared repository supports distinct research stages rather than establishing a fully autonomous experimental discovery pipeline.

name: PaperOrchestra
summary: Turns supplied ideas and experimental records into LaTeX manuscripts using planning, literature, plotting, writing, and refinement agents. On a benchmark reconstructed from 200 accepted papers, human reviewers prefer its drafts to two writing baselines. These comparisons assess manuscript quality; citation-identity checks and simulated acceptance do not validate underlying science, and generated figures and model-driven refinement require independent review.

name: AutoIllustrate
summary: Converts a method description into an editable draw.io diagram, then optionally applies an image-generation restyling pass. The public command-line workflow includes figure generation and visual auditing and was used with Agentic Scientist. Retaining the vector source supports manual correction, but generated visual polish should not be taken as evidence of methodological fidelity.

name: PaperBanana
summary: Uses retrieval, planning, styling, visualization, and critique agents to generate academic diagrams and plots from scientific content. Its repository includes execution interfaces and a benchmark of reference illustrations. It is a useful study of iterative visual communication, with semantic accuracy and faithful representation of experimental data still requiring inspection beyond aesthetic judgments.
status: Published at ICML 2026 (PMLR 306). The final paper and substantive appendices were appraised; illustration and plot evaluations do not certify every generated technical detail.

name: PaperQA2
summary: Searches papers iteratively, summarizes and reranks evidence, traverses citations, and produces cited answers. LitQA2 evaluation finds higher answer precision than human annotators, with comparable overall accuracy. WikiCrow and ContraCrow extend the approach to summaries and contradiction screening; human agreement depends on the evidence and reasoning shown. The evaluated configuration and accessible full-text corpus differ from a default open-package installation.

name: OpenScholar
summary: A scientific-literature synthesis system combining specialized retrieval, reranking, citation-linked generation and iterative feedback. The author-linked preprint evaluates answer quality, attribution and expert preference across several disciplines, while documenting persistent factuality and retrieval limitations. Human preference chiefly reflects coverage and presentation, rather than independently verified correctness. The later Nature publication is linked by the authors, but its main text and supplements remain unread in this audit.

name: STORM / Co-STORM
summary: STORM develops cited articles through perspective-guided questions, web-grounded conversations, and outline refinement. Its Co-STORM companion lets users steer simulated-expert discussions and organizes findings in a shared mind map. Evaluations support aspects of organization and user preference; small human studies and model-based grading do not establish objective learning gains, complete factual accuracy, or publication-ready scientific reporting.

name: ASReview LAB
summary: Uses active learning to prioritize records during systematic literature screening while preserving human inclusion decisions. It provides a screening interface, simulation tools, label management, and exportable review state. This is a complementary evidence-selection tool rather than a generative scientist; screening completeness depends on the review protocol, labels, and stopping decision.

name: GPT Researcher
summary: A configurable research agent that decomposes questions, gathers evidence from web or local sources, and assembles cited reports. It exposes a package, interfaces, and multi-agent or recursive research workflows. It is useful as a general research component, but its project-level claims should not be confused with scientific novelty or independently validated literature-review completeness.

name: AIDE
summary: Searches executable ML solutions through draft, debug, and improvement branches scored by a supplied metric. Author Kaggle experiments and separately reported MLE-Bench/RE-Bench evaluations support bounded engineering utility. Historical leaderboard comparisons use differing holdouts and retain contamination risks; task-level labels in one table conflict with its definition. Results depend on model, budget, evaluator, and search space, and do not establish autonomous selection of scientific questions.

name: R&D-Agent
summary: A modular framework for autonomous machine-learning engineering that separates idea search from implementation and feedback. Its tested agent combines adaptive parallel exploration, structured hypothesis generation, collaborative memory, sampled-data debugging and standardized solution selection. MLE-Bench experiments report competition-medal gains with matched ML-Master reruns and selected-subset ablations. The evidence concerns bounded data-science optimization, with historical comparisons subject to differing models, hardware and budgets.

name: ShinkaEvolve
summary: Evolves programs against human-defined executable objectives using island archives, language-model mutations, novelty rejection, and adaptive model selection. Experiments cover circle packing, AIME scaffolds, ALE-Bench solutions, and MoE load balancing. Reported gains are task-dependent: exact circle-packing validation requires postprocessing, and the AIME 2025 scaffold trails majority voting. Open code supports local or cluster evaluation.
status: ICLR 2026 publication identity verified. The complete original preprint was appraised; changes in the inaccessible final paper and supplement remain unverified.

name: OpenEvolve
summary: An open community implementation inspired by AlphaEvolve that evolves programs using language models, evaluator feedback, and population-based search. It includes examples for mathematical optimization, scientific computing, and kernel improvement. The repository is independently maintained rather than Google's original system, and its reported improvements should be checked against the corresponding evaluator and hardware conditions.

name: ToolUniverse
summary: Provides a common interface for scientific tools, datasets, models, and APIs so language-model agents can discover and invoke external capabilities. The public project offers a Python SDK and agent integrations. It supplies infrastructure for building scientific assistants; available tool connectors do not by themselves establish reliable tool selection, valid analyses, or experimental reproducibility.

name: Docling
summary: Converts documents into structured representations using page-layout analysis, table reconstruction, optional OCR, and typed assembly. Its technical report benchmarks runtime on five documents totaling 225 pages with OCR disabled, rather than establishing general extraction accuracy. Published examples omit figure text and break a cross-column paragraph; Markdown repeats spanning headers while JSON retains spans. Current software capabilities should be checked separately from this historical report.

name: Recursive Eureka Machine
summary: Recursive describes an automated research loop that proposes ideas, implements experiments, checks results, and carries useful context across parallel investigations. Public examples include training and GPU-kernel optimization; its later Flint model provides a released development outcome. Available research artifacts support inspection of selected outputs, but do not establish access to the complete research framework or independently verified autonomy.
status: Creator-reported system; public output artifacts are distinct from full framework source.

name: Recursive Flint
summary: An open-weight mixture-of-experts coding model built with Recursive’s Eureka Machine and a human team. The model card specifies 39.8B total parameters and approximately 2.5B active per token, including the output head. Included as a concrete automated-research output and reusable coding component; released weights and inference code do not independently validate the development process or reported performance.
status: Apache-2.0 weights and inference engine; no local execution or independent performance reproduction in this collection.

name: DiscoveryRSI
summary: Provides a public research harness with provider adapters, role prompts, a tool registry, replay storage, and domain adapters for hypothesis development. The accompanying DiscoveryRSI-27B checkpoint supports research planning and revision. Public components expose the workflow, but restricted datasets and private campaign traces are excluded; this collection has not executed the system.

name: RIDAR
summary: Provides trajectory collectors, post-hoc integrity detection, runtime intervention, and a monitoring interface for research agents. Findings link to evidence in recorded runs, with public result files accompanying the implementation. It supports investigation of agent research behavior; detector output requires contextual review and does not certify scientific validity.
status: Official repository announces the code release on 23 October. No installation or runtime validation was performed here.

name: PDE-GAV
summary: Provides a configurable PDE experimentation environment with public-input queries, private reference evaluation, candidate selection, run logs, and interfaces for new equations and tasks. The repository documents a deterministic CPU demonstration and scientific campaign configurations. Large datasets, weights, and complete historical execution archives are external; public code availability alone does not reproduce the paper’s experiments.
status: Official repository and documentation inspected without installation or execution. Only the release year is recorded; a precise initial software-release date was not established.

name: Magnolia
summary: Adds readable project notebooks, reviewed memory promotion, scientific-tool wrappers, and local or Slurm job tracking to an OpenCode-based workflow. Two MCP services expose memory and computational operations while preserving run provenance. Researchers direct the work and approve standing rules; the claim critic and promotion panel do not establish scientific correctness, and adaptation to another harness requires additional integration.
status: Public research software; no installation or execution was performed. The paper explicitly disclaims autonomy, so the catalog treats this as supporting research infrastructure. Precise initial release date not established.

name: OpenScientist
summary: Runs iterative investigations from researcher questions and optional datasets, combining executable analysis, PubMed retrieval, hypothesis tracking, persistent research state, and final reports. The inspected code supports feedback between iterations and database-backed knowledge records. Public source supports inspection and self-hosting; the biomedical preprint evaluates an earlier configuration, and recorded findings or matched citations do not independently establish scientific validity.
status: Implementation inspected at commit 9513b998cea5 without execution. The year identifies the documented 2026 implementation, not an established first public release date. The hosted service was not tested.

name: PaperScorer
summary: Packages manuscript preparation, acceptance scoring, an agent-assisted review interface, and optional literature reranking behind a command-line orchestrator. It accepts PDFs, LaTeX projects, or arXiv identifiers and supports comparison across manuscript commits. Released source enables inspection; score changes describe predicted review outcomes, and generated critiques still require evidence checking rather than being treated as validated scientific judgments.
status: MIT-licensed implementation and documentation inspected at f76d60e4e051 without installation or model execution. The repository links model and dataset releases; those artifacts were not downloaded. Precise initial software-release date was not established.

name: ClaimNov
summary: Provides reusable claim extraction, reference-pool retrieval, entailment scoring, and proposal verdict functions. Reports retain matched papers and claim-level evidence, while evaluation scripts support comparison with existing novelty checks. Researchers supply the prior-work pool and model services. Scores describe coverage by that pool; they neither certify universal novelty nor validate scientific correctness.
status: README and pipeline inspected at 413f16c7f94b without installation or model calls. Precise initial software-release date was not established.

name: MUSE
summary: Provides memory construction, consolidation, retrieval, and gate components with prompts and structured schemas. A scientific coding agent supplies the task and tool interactions; the gate can return focused review advice or skip injection. The release supports integration and inspection, while benchmark environments and verifiers are separate dependencies. Component availability does not by itself reproduce the paper’s full evaluation.
status: Public README and component tree inspected at 524ddcd70fa5 without installation, model calls, or benchmark execution. Precise initial software-release date was not established.

name: Claim-to-evidence checker
summary: Extracts numerical result claims, indexes recorded result files, and compares value matches with contextual provenance scores and per-claim decoys. Frozen operating points support certification and audit outputs. It is useful for reviewing research reports against their saved artifacts; unsupported matches need contextual review, and incomplete logs or extraction failures can leave correct claims uncertified.
status: Public checker tree and README inspected at e6253daa687e without execution. The repository releases derived data and labels rather than redistributing the benchmark’s raw submissions. Precise initial software-release date was not established.

name: SpectralColorLab
summary: Supplies Windows acquisition software, Android AR stimulus control, and iPad USB/SSH helpers for acknowledged color holds and spectrometer sampling. Synthetic RGB definitions support reconstructing stimulus protocols; calibrated hardware and vendor SDKs must be provided separately. Useful for building inspectable measurement interfaces. Released source excludes observed measurements, fitted models, and calibration, so software availability does not reproduce the optical results or establish a complete recursive research-agent framework.
status: Source and README inspected at 255a2f896040 without installation or execution. The represented software is from 2026; a precise first-public-release date was not established. Device acknowledgements verify rendering state, not calibrated optical emission or physical settling.

name: DefectSkills
summary: Provides reusable prompts, human decision points, and optional reference scripts for VASP-based point-defect calculations. The public release contains the workflow manuscript and supporting analysis files; running it requires a configured scientific-computing environment and appropriate VASP access. It is guidance for an agent, rather than a standalone autonomous engine, and the reported demonstration still required scientific and execution corrections.

name: auto_research (high-energy astrophysics)
summary: Public orchestration code connects research agents to a separate analysis toolkit, checks generated tools, and validates report provenance. Tool changes enter a working branch; trusted promotion remains a human decision. The documented deployment needs configured model services and astronomy software. Source availability supports inspection, while the paper’s event logs and planted-defect review records are request-only and no execution was performed for this collection.

name: AIDE (scientific data curation)
summary: Public data-curation pipeline searches Hugging Face datasets, applies a model-based quality gate, and generates processing code for retrieval or instruction formats. The documented outputs retain selected sources, processors, organized data, and logs; paper evaluations use separate downstream tools. This is the Agentic Intelligent Data Engine, distinct from WecoAI’s AIDE search agent. Model services and data access are required for full curation; no runtime was executed here.

name: Computational Discovery (Google Labs)
summary: Hosted scientific-coding tool built with ERA and AlphaEvolve, announced through Google’s trusted-tester program. The November 2026 update documents MCP integration for approved users alongside browser access. It offers a route to delegate computational investigations from compatible agents; access is gated, and the collection did not use the service. Published ERA research and generated application artifacts should be distinguished from availability or independent validation of this hosted product.

name: NORA (spatial data science)
summary: Coordinates spatial research through domain skills, persistent project files, separate reviewers, and nine human checkpoints. Three cases demonstrate workflow assistance with substantive expert intervention; human rigor ratings are lower than model ratings, and ablations are qualitative. Generated reports retain validation problems, including an invalid fairness-bound argument, so completed workflows require independent scientific checking.

name: Brilliance
summary: Public conversational accelerator-research framework connects agent-written Python programs to JuTrack numerical services, reusable expert modules, and persistent project evidence. The documented installation requires Julia, scientific dependencies, and a configured model backend. Scientists can inspect calculations and redirect investigations. The paper evaluates simulation and offline measured-response calibration; neither source availability nor the example gallery demonstrates independent reproduction or live accelerator operation.

name: BVSR discovery toolkit
summary: Provides public modules for literature-grounded proposal generation, creativity labeling, selector training and SimpleTES integration. The default reproduction path rebuilds tables and figures from released outcomes; rerun mode still reuses frozen baselines, judge rankings and selector datasets. Fresh runs require model/API resources, GPU components and gated dependencies. Documentation and the source inventory were inspected at a pinned revision. Execution and scientific reproduction were not tested.
status: Year-only software date: the inspected revision is dated 10 November 2026, but the first public release day was not established. Stored-result reconstruction and fresh experimentation remain distinct.
